rates_source.title: Bloesch and Weber, "Structural Changes in Investment and the Waning Power of Monetary Policy", Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Reports no. 1190, March 2026
rates_source.quote: the response of residential investment, non-residential structures, and equipment which peak at 15, 5, and 10 percent, respectively
rates_source.shock: The effect of a 1% decrease in the federal funds rate on real investment

rates_caveats: The 5% is the peak response of nonresidential structures SPENDING to a 100 bp CUT. Applying it to bookings, and to a rise, assumes the effect is symmetric. That is an assumption.
In that paper the spending response peaks about 10 quarters after the shock. Bookings lead spending, so the 6-month lag on bookings is an assumption.
The estimate uses 1969 to 1996 data, and Chicago Fed Letter 482 (2023) reports a positive response of structures to higher rates, which it calls puzzling. The sign is not settled.

episodes.basis: From the last month before the first 2025 metals action to the latest month in the snapshot. It reflects current tariff levels, so it is the default. Over a 19-month window the price change also includes global price and demand moves, so treat it as the larger estimate.
